stem: Set A has 5 elements and set B has 3 elements. All elements of B are also in A. How many elements does A ∪ B contain?

per_option_rationale.rationale: B is a subset of A, so A ∪ B = A, which has 5 elements.
Student adds |A| + |B| = 5 + 3 = 8, ignoring that the elements of B are already counted in A.
Student reports |B| = 3, confusing union with intersection when B is a subset of A.
Student computes |A| - |B| = 5 - 3 = 2, applying a difference formula instead of union.

explanation: Because B is a subset of A, every element of B is already in A. The union A ∪ B equals A, so it contains 5 elements.

explanation_sections.punchline: B is a subset of A, so A ∪ B = A. The union adds nothing new and contains exactly 5 elements.
explanation_sections.approach: Union questions require checking subset relationships before applying the inclusion-exclusion formula. If one set is entirely inside the other, the union equals the larger set. Check subset status first, then decide whether a formula is even needed.
explanation_sections.lesson: When B is a subset of A, A ∪ B = A and |A ∪ B| = |A|. Adding the sizes only works when the sets share no elements at all.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60 seconds. Recognise the subset condition in the stem in under 10 seconds and write the answer. Eliminate option 8 first: it assumes zero overlap.
